_doc: Tello camera model applied to the sim's capture frames (sim/tello_cam.py, used by sim/frames.py and sim/yolo_check.py). Every number is a guess until scripts/sim_real_gap.py --fit is run on a real Tello recording. ?cam=raw on the sim URL turns it off.

lens._doc: dist (OpenCV k1 k2 p1 p2 k3) comes from data/tello_camera.json when it exists and has one; this one is the community Tello calibration (fx 921, fy 919) copied around Tello ArUco projects, not ours. render_fx is the sim's own focal length (sim/src/config.ts FX): distortion is applied around it, so the field of view doesn't change. softness_sigma_px: the Tello picture is soft (ISP + H.264), a Gaussian blur.

vignette._doc: brightness falls to (1 - strength) at the corners, quadratic in radius

exposure._doc: auto-exposure: a gain that pulls mean luma toward target_luma with time constant adapt_s. exposure_ms sets the motion blur length.

noise._doc: sensor noise in 0-255 units before the ISP: sigma = sqrt(shot * value + read^2)

motion_blur._doc: horizontal smear of fx * yaw_rate * exposure_ms from the camera's turn rate (pose heading)

rolling_shutter._doc: rows read top to bottom over readout_ms: a turning camera skews verticals

color._doc: Tello looks washed out and a bit green: per-channel gains (R, G, B), saturation (1 = unchanged), contrast around mid-grey, a lifted black level, then gamma

compression._doc: H.264 at the Tello's few Mbit/s stands in as one JPEG pass (8x8 DCT quantisation) at this quality

stream._doc: Wi-Fi video link: every frame arrives latency_ms late (uniform in the range), some are dropped, some repeat the previous frame
